claim_ceiling: Synthetic conformance corpus for an independent Directory Fabric effect-history checker. No oracle test, benchmark, database, broker, or fault-injection result is executed or qualified.
core_rule: Incomplete, missing, unauthenticated, or contradictory evidence must never be coerced into VALID.

scenarios.description: Effect obtains and commits under the old owner fence before the fence transaction commits; owner acknowledgement follows durable read-back.
An old-generation effect commits at a later owner-local sequence after the new fence commit.
One required owner stream is not complete in the supplied evidence bundle.
Two event records reuse the same event identity.
An event references a causal parent omitted from the evidence bundle.
The same owner-scoped logical operation commits more than one protected effect.
The global acknowledgement omits one required owner acknowledgement.
A physical effect attempt remains Unknown without exact terminal reconciliation.
A new route is admitted after a global barrier using an exact current inventory mapping, atomic owner fence and durable owner read-back.
A route with best-effort or signal-only enforcement is activated into strict execution.
A worker with a superseded claim epoch commits after a newer claim was installed in the owner stream.
The causal DAG orders a later owner-local durable sequence before an earlier one.
A new physical attempt starts while the preceding attempt remains Unknown and has no ConfirmedNoEffect reconciliation.
The exact immediately preceding attempt is independently reconciled as terminal ConfirmedNoEffect before the retry starts.
A route ID is paired with an owner different from the exact route-to-owner mapping in the verified inventory.
One owner acknowledgement binds a different inventory epoch or manifest from the global acknowledgement.
The same owner-scoped idempotency key commits two distinct logical operations.
An owner-local effect commit substitutes a different effect owner from the owner bound by its exact attempt and worker claim.
A post-barrier route inventory closure binds a different revocation identity from the global barrier whose owner read-back it attempts to reuse.

comparator_methods: Porcupine executable sequential model and concurrent history linearizability checking
Jepsen-style captured history, fault injection and independent consistency checking
Mycelix domain-specific oracle over owner epochs, exact route inventory, worker claims, durable fence/read-back chains and global barrier receipts
evidence_requirements: exact checker source SHA and binary digest
raw input event bundle and corpus digest
ingestion adapter source/build digest and completeness evidence
all verdicts and finding codes, including INCONCLUSIVE
per-run raw timing and peak-memory samples
reproducible random seeds and fault schedule
no dropped failed histories or omitted inconclusive runs
